title: Multimodal traffic orchestration and rollback latency budget — scratchpad
body:
Purpose
Quick working notes and experiment scaffolding for orchestrating canaries that touch multiple inference surfaces (text generation, embeddings, image->caption, and reranking pipelines) while guaranteeing a rollback path that preserves our latency budget and keeps cost growth bounded. This is intentionally rough — operational checklist + escalation playbook + unanswered questions.

Context and problem statement
- We now have hybrid features that fan out across different model classes: e.g., a single API call that triggers ranking (reranker), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) + multimodal preprocessing. Small changes can spike cost or tail latency in one surface and silently degrade user-facing latency.
- Current canaries are single-surface and assume symmetric signal cadence. Multi-surface canaries need coordinated signals, a single orchestrated kill-switch, and cost-aware gating to avoid runaway GPUs.

Goals
1) Define a minimal telemetry contract for each surface to be included in a cross-surface canary.
2) Provide a deterministic decision tree for progressive exposure that bounds 95th and 99th percentile latency within an agreed budget.
3) Offer explicit, low-friction rollback mechanisms (automated + manual) and a cost-rate limiter as a fallback.
4) Document experiments to validate the above in staging and a constrained pilot cohort.

Telemetry contract (minimal required signals)
- Common fields (per request): trace_id, customer_id (hashed), route, canary_tag, timestamp, request_size_tokens, response_size_tokens, seq_length, model_variant, region.
- Surface-specific: 
  - Text generation: per-token latency (first token, median token, last token), kv-cache-hit (bool), batch_id.
  - Embeddings: encode_time_ms, cpu_preprocess_ms, gpu_compute_ms, vector_norm.
  - Reranker: upstream_latency_ms, candidate_count, scoring_time_ms, top_k_returned.
  - Multimodal preprocess (vision): image_decode_ms, resize_ms, augmentations_applied (list), OCR_time_ms (if enabled).
- Derived metrics to compute in telemetry pipeline: request end-to-end latency, cost_estimate_usd (apply model and sequence length unit costs), tail_latency_95/99, error_rate (per-surface and aggregate), fraction_of_requests_using_fallback_route.

Decision tree for progressive exposure (sketch)
- Phase 0: shadow — route 100% production traffic to canary shadow path but zero impact on responses (observe telemetry only). Run at least 72h or N requests where N is 10k or customer-weighted-equivalent.
- Phase 1: very small live cohort (0.1% global, or specific internal test cohort). Enable full response path but with client-visible flag (for internal customers / dogfood).
- Phase 2: burst window gating — allow bursts up to X rps for Y minutes, enforce strict cost-rate limiter (see below). Observe SLOs for 6–12 hours.
- Phase 3: incremental ramp — 1% -> 5% -> 20% over days, require green checks at each step (latency, error, cost).
- Abort criteria (immediate rollback): any of the following computed on last 5-minute window:
  - Aggregate error_rate > 2x baseline and absolute > 0.5%
  - End-to-end p99 increases > 2x baseline (or exceeds configured absolute p99 budget)
  - Cost_estimate rate > 3x projected allowed spend rate for canary cohort
  - Any data-exfiltration / PII detection alarms triggered in preprocessing pipeline

Operational guardrails and quick revert paths
- Single orchestrated kill-switch: orchestrator should be able to toggle canary_tag -> fallback route in one API call (and via console). Implementation: route rewrite at ingress that sends canary-tagged traffic to stable model graph.
- Cost rate limiter: token-per-second budget per canary that, when exceeded, triggers degraded mode where we: 1) reduce max_tokens output, 2) limit candidate_count in reranker, 3) fallback to smaller quantized model for embeddings.
- Fast revert runbook (for oncall):
  1) Execute: POST /orchestrator/v1/canary_controls/{canary_id}/deactivate -> returns revert_token.
  2) Verify traffic rewrite: query /observability/route_snapshot?trace_id=latest -> expect stable_model graph.
  3) Raise incident with subject: [CANARY REVERT] {canary_id} — include last 3 telemetry snapshots, last 100 traces.
  4) If revert fails, enable global cost-rate limiter: POST /quota/v1/global/consume_override with payload {"action": "cut_tokens", "pct": 50}.

Human-in-the-loop scheduling
- Assign a steward for each cross-surface canary (rotation 1 week). Steward responsibilities: kickoff, weekday monitoring window 1300–1800 PT on ramp days, ensure pager handoff.
- Communication channels: #canary-alpha (ops), escalation to oncall-sre if revert needed. Use templated messages (copy/paste):
  - Pre-ramp: "Starting ramp: {canary_id}, cohort {slice}, expected duration {hours}, steward {name}, observability links: {dashboards}."
  - Abort: "Aborting {canary_id}. Reason: {primary_signal}. Revert token: {token}. Actions taken: traffic rewrote, tickets created: {jira}."

Testing matrix to validate the plan (staging first)
- Test 1: Synthetic surge across surfaces simultaneously — generate blended workload (50% text gen, 30% embeddings, 20% rerank/vision) at 5x expected normal RPS for 30 minutes. Validate: p95/p99 in stage < 1.5x prod baseline, no memory thrashing, no OOMs.
- Test 2: Cost ramp simulation — increase sequence lengths and batch sizes to push cost_estimate_usd to 3x baseline and observe that cost-rate limiter enforces degradations automatically.
- Test 3: Failure injection — simulate slow preprocessing (vision decode + OCR delayed) and ensure orchestrator rolls back within configured time or triggers fallback model.
- Test 4: Data guardrail trip — inject synthetic PII into requests and make sure detection pipeline flags and triggers immediate halt.

Metrics dashboards and alerts (practical suggestions)
- Per-canary dashboard tiles: composite end-to-end latency (p50/p95/p99), per-surface p95/p99, aggregate cost rate per minute, error_rate (by surface), fallback_fraction, batch_size_distribution, kv-cache-hit-rate.
- Short-window alerts (5m): p99 > budget OR cost_rate > threshold -> page steward and SRE.
- Longer window alerts (1h): sustained p95 increase or cost drift -> auto create incident and mark canary degraded.

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self)
- How to compute a defensible cost_estimate_usd in near-real-time that accounts for mixed hardware pools (some requests hit cheaper instances)? Need input from infra/cost. Action: sync with Luis on cost telemetry mapping (Linear INF-1124).
- Per-customer isolation: should high-risk customers be excluded from early ramp cohorts by default? Might need rule-based cohort selection.
- Console UX: quick revert should show a single button but also surface the last 10 offending traces inline. Is that feasible without exposing trace payloads? Privacy question.
- Validation criteria for phase jumps: exact numerical thresholds (p95 delta, error absolutes) need to be agreed with product and SRE.

Notes from last sync (11/20 retro)
- Priya: prefer conservative p99 thresholds for multimodal features; users notice tail latency even if p50 is great.
- Ethan: implement cost-rate limiter as first line of defense rather than immediate revert — less noisy and more predictable.
- Maya: set up a canary smoke synthetic user that exercises all surfaces in a single trace for easier debugging.

Appendix: quick CLI snippets (ops)
- Toggle canary off:
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
    https://orchestrator.redwood.internal/v1/canary_controls/my-canary/deactivate

- Query recent traces for canary:
  curl -s "https://observability.internal/api/traces?tag=canary:my-canary&limit=100" | jq .

- Apply cost cut: (emergency)
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN" 
    -d '{"action":"cut_tokens","pct":50}' https://quota.redwood.internal/v1/overrides

End of scratchpad — keep terse, add experiments and thresholds as we get SRE + infra numbers.
